stop_condition: Both round-1 HIGH repairs are verified by my own counterexamples, the elision policy is judged honest as a reviewer receiving it, and no unresolved finding at or above high remains in the gate machinery.

findings.evidence: THE R1-F1 REPAIR IS DEFEATED BY ONE INHERITED ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE, reproduced end to end against the shipped runner with a matched control. bd 1.2.2 honours BOTH spellings and BD_ACTOR WINS: with both set in one call, 'BD_ACTOR=aaa-bd-wins BEADS_ACTOR=zzz-beads-wins bd comment ...' recorded 'bd: comment (auto-commit) by aaa-bd-wins [...]' — measured directly in an mktemp store. So an inherited BD_ACTOR overrides the runner's marker, no commit can ever carry it, and every self-contamination is attributed external. DEMONSTRATED, not inferred (scratchpad/probe-bdactor.sh, same derived-id contaminator as R1-F1, two fixtures, one variable different): CONTROL with BD_ACTOR unset -> 'Total: 1  Passed: 0  Failed: 1', 'zz-contaminator.sh: FAILED', present in the Failed tests list. WITH BD_ACTOR=alice -> 'Total: 1  Passed: 1  Failed: 0', 'zz-contaminator.sh: PASSED but DEGRADED (... externally attributed to alice ...)', absent from the Failed tests list. The fixture's own dolt log confirms the mechanism: 'bd: comment (auto-commit) by alice [fx-bdactor-...]' — the marker never appears. (Methodology note on my own probe: its printed RESULT line keyed off rc and said 'no bypass', which is WRONG — rc is confounded by the completeness-floor breach in a small fixture. The per-spec verdict and the Failed count are the uncontaminated discriminators and both flip. I am reporting the corrected reading, not the probe's own summary.) CONFIRMED ABSENT: 'grep -n BD_ACTOR .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh' returns NOTHING — the runner neither unsets nor sets it — and the ACTOR-MARKER block (read in full, :210-256) sets and exports the marker with no round-trip self-check, so nothing anywhere notices that the marker did not take effect. LATENT, NOT LIVE: BD_ACTOR is not set in my environment, not in the repo, and not in .github/workflows/test.yml. But bd's OWN config.yaml comment names BD_ACTOR — the implementer recorded that docs contradiction in its notes — so an operator following bd's own documentation sets precisely the variable that silently disables this canary.
findings.description: R1-F1 restored in full, silently and totally: Failed: 1 becomes Failed: 0 for an identical contaminating spec. The repair is otherwise excellent and I verified it works (my round-1 counterexample now FAILS, named, and runner-completeness 13i/13m/13j/13k cover the whole matrix) — but its correctness rests on an unverified assumption about bd's env-var precedence, and that assumption is false. This is the same class the fix was praised for eliminating: a mechanism assumed effective rather than proven effective. REQUIRED FIX, in order of preference: (a) an ARM-TIME SELF-CHECK — after exporting the marker, perform one throwaway write to a scratch store and assert the recorded actor equals the marker; if it does not, set STORE_CANARY_DISARM_REASON and DISARM loudly. The disarm machinery already exists and already prints on every run, so this costs a few lines and is immune to whatever bd does next with variable names, because it tests behaviour rather than encoding a belief about precedence. (b) Failing that, 'unset BD_ACTOR' alongside the export (BD_ACTOR wins, so unsetting it makes BEADS_ACTOR authoritative), or export both to the same value. (a) is strongly preferred: (b) encodes today's precedence as an assumption, which is exactly what went wrong here.

findings.evidence: The R1-F2 repair is a real improvement and I verified both tautology guards are genuine: 19c.3/19c.4/19c.5 statically assert the declaration contains no backtick substitution, no $TESTS_DIR and no $PROJECT_DIR (I independently grepped the whole array body for '$(', backticks, 'find', $TESTS_DIR and $PROJECT_DIR — CLEAN); 19d splices in a genuinely self-deriving declaration and proves the four-leg pairing (19d.3 precondition, 19d.4 the mutant still exits 0 with an undeclared 4th spec, 19d.5 reports 'floor HELD', 19d.7 the shipped runner exits non-zero over the same fixture). I counted 72 declared array ELEMENTS (line-anchored regex, not lines mentioning) against 72 discovered by the runner's own query. BUT THE TRIGGER IS STILL CARDINALITY: the set difference (DECLARED_BASENAMES / DISCOVERED_BASENAMES / 'comm -13') is computed only INSIDE the count-mismatch branch, to explain which specs differ. REPRODUCED with a control (scratchpad/probe-compensating.sh, using the same EXPECTED-SPEC-FILES sentinel splice 19d uses): a mutant declaring exactly {stub-001, stub-002, stub-003}. CONTROL, honest 3/3 on disk -> rc=0, 'Completeness floor: HELD (3/3 ...)' as expected. PROBE, stub-003.sh declared but ABSENT and zz-undeclared.sh present but NOT declared, count still 3 vs 3 -> rc=0, 'Completeness floor: HELD (3/3 ...)'. A declared spec vanished and an undeclared one ran, and the floor reported HELD.
findings.description: A compensating add-plus-remove is invisible. The ordinary operation that produces exactly this shape is a RENAME ('git mv foo.test.sh bar.test.sh' without touching the array): count unchanged, so the array now declares a file that does not exist while an undeclared file runs, and nothing says so. This is NOT a regression — neither the old integer nor the new array caught it — and the array is a genuine improvement for the pure-add and pure-remove cases the coordinator filed it for. FIX, at zero extra cost because the data is already in hand: compute DECLARED/DISCOVERED and the two-way 'comm' UNCONDITIONALLY, and breach on a non-empty symmetric difference rather than on a count mismatch. The count then becomes a derived convenience rather than the predicate. Worth folding into qist rather than spawning a new task.

findings.evidence: I was asked to judge this AS THE REVIEWER RECEIVING THE PACKET, so I measured what I would actually be handed. ASSEMBLED FOR REAL, this round, iteration 2: 81866 bytes total (under the 100000 cap), diff_total_bytes 322780, 8 of 17 files included, 9 omitted. WHAT I RECEIVED IN FULL: backend.md, designer.md, devops.md, frontend.md, orchestrator.md, qa.md, lessons.sh, LESSONS.md. WHAT I DID NOT RECEIVE: qa-gate.sh (48868 bytes, tier 1), verify-before-stop.sh (19895, tier 1), run-tests.sh (42784), review-request-build.test.sh (39021), runner-completeness.test.sh (36371), next-work.test.sh (33755), review-request-diff-budget.test.sh (28460), lessons.test.sh (20248), and my own r1 artifact. So the packet contained ZERO of the code implementing either HIGH repair, and zero of the elision feature being reviewed, while containing six agent prompts this batch barely touched. THE POLICY CHOICE IS NOT A WASH, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS DECISIVE. Budget = REVIEW_REQUEST_DIFF_TARGET_BYTES(80000) - spec - contract - impact - FIXED_OVERHEAD(1500); I verified this exactly (80000 - 37806 - 2830 - 1566 - 1500 = 36298, the budget the run reported). Max achievable budget, with a zero-byte contract, is 80000 - 0 - 2830 - 1566 - 1500 = 74104. Under smallest-first the small-file floor is 35841 bytes, so qa-gate.sh can NEVER be included: 35841 + 48868 = 84709 > 74104, at any contract size. Under largest-first, qa-gate.sh + verify-before-stop.sh = 68763 < 74104 — BOTH tier-1 scripts fit, and the six prompts are what gets dropped instead. IS THE PACKET HONEST? YES, unambiguously, and I want that recorded as clearly as the criticism: elision is whole-file-only (E.3/E.5 prove no fragment leaks), every omission is named with path, exact bytes and tier IN THE RENDERED DIFF TEXT rather than only on the envelope, the text states plainly 'this diff is INCOMPLETE' and says how to recover each path, and the accounting invariant holds on the real packet — I checked it myself twice: 35841 + 286939 = 322780, and after my contract change 55736 + 267044 = 322780. F.3 meta-tests that invariant against a stubbed zero-omitted claim. It does NOT cross the line the brief drew: a reviewer cannot form an UNKNOWING confident verdict on this packet.
findings.description: My judgment, since it was asked for: the elision mechanism is honest and well-built, and smallest-first is the wrong default. It optimises the number of complete files shown; review risk concentrates in change VOLUME, which is exactly what it discards, so it systematically omits the highest-risk files. On this packet that is not a marginal effect — it deterministically excluded 100% of tier-1 source and 100% of tests. RECOMMENDED: largest-first within a tier, or reserve a fraction of the budget for the largest tier-1 file so the single biggest behavioural change is always shown. SECOND, AND ARGUABLY MORE IMPORTANT THAN THE ORDERING: when any tier-1 file is omitted, the packet should say so in instruction form, not only in fact form — something the reviewer must act on, e.g. 'N tier-1 source file(s) were omitted; you cannot assess them and must not return verdict=approve on their behalf.' The facts are all present; what is missing is any pressure on the reviewer to treat them as disqualifying. That is the residual risk: not that the packet lies, but that an approve-shaped artifact about six documentation files could enter the audit trail labelled as a review of this change set.

findings.evidence: THE RELAY WAS ATTEMPTED, AS DIRECTED, AND THIS IS THE RESULT. Lane codex (handshake, gpt-5.6-sol). Packet assembled at 77880 bytes — UNDER the 100000 cap, so the exit-7 refusal correctly did NOT fire, which is the R1-F4 fix working exactly as designed. The driver accepted it, spawned the real Codex MCP server, and Sol engaged: 'node .../codex -m gpt-5.6-sol mcp-server' ran for the FULL budget (measured 40:0x elapsed on the driver pid). Outcome: rc=5, '[codex-review] codex tool call exceeded the 2400s wall-clock budget — the server was STILL ALIVE at the deadline (id=2 never answered; Sol was still generating); no artifact'. NO artifact was produced and nothing entered the tree (git status unchanged at 50 entries, tracker unchanged at 17, change_set_hash still 039fa5d8...). WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ONE FAILED CALL: .claude/review-config's own rationale for the 100000 cap records exactly two measurements — a ~88KB request that COMPLETED in 326s, 493s, 496s, 613s and 635s across five separate rounds, and a ~144KB request that exhausted the whole 2400s budget — and states, admirably, that 'deriving a relationship needs a third measurement at minimum, which does not exist yet'. This is that third measurement, and it does not fit: 77880 bytes is roughly 12% SMALLER than the packet that completed five times out of five, and it exhausted the entire budget. So SIZE IS NOT THE CONTROLLING VARIABLE, and max_request_bytes cannot be relied upon to prevent the 40-minute dead end it was introduced to prevent. HONEST CAVEATS: N=1 for my point; Sol latency varies; and my packet's CONTENT (a 17-file gate-machinery change set, a 2830-byte multi-criterion spec, and a 9-file omission list) plausibly costs more generation time than an equally-sized simpler packet — which is itself the point, since the cap measures bytes and not that.
findings.description: The diagnosis side of this driver is excellent and I want to credit it precisely: the fkm.1.14 fold-in did its job, distinguishing 'server STILL ALIVE, still generating' from 'server exited' and naming the unanswered request id. That is the difference between a diagnosable failure and the original silent dead end. What does not work is the PREVENTION: a byte cap chosen by interpolating two points cannot bound a quantity that is not a function of bytes. RECOMMENDED, and none of these is mine to choose: (a) add a first-response/liveness deadline much shorter than the total budget so a non-answering call fails in minutes rather than at 40, since 'still generating at 2400s' was knowable far earlier; (b) record this third data point in review-config's rationale regardless of what else changes, because the file's own text invites it and a future maintainer will otherwise re-derive the same wrong curve; (c) revisit chunking, which R1-F4 deferred as an open question and which this result makes the only approach that has not yet been falsified. MY ROUND-1 POSITION IS REINFORCED RATHER THAN OVERTURNED: an honest exit 7 costs nothing, whereas the alternative just cost a full 40-minute paid budget and produced no artifact and no review.

findings.evidence: Packet composition is highly sensitive to the size of fields that are not the diff, and nothing warns the caller. Demonstrated by me this round: with the union completion contract at 37806 bytes the budget was 36298 and verify-before-stop.sh was OMITTED; I reassembled with a deliberately slimmed contract at 13603 bytes and the budget grew enough that verify-before-stop.sh became INCLUDED (9 files, 55736 bytes, invariant 55736 + 267044 = 322780 still exact). Same change set, same code, different review coverage — decided entirely by how verbose the caller's completion-contract file happened to be.
findings.description: Not a defect so much as an unflagged coupling: the contract, the spec and the impact summary compete with the diff for one 80000-byte target, and the diff is the only one of the four a reviewer cannot obtain elsewhere. The envelope already reports diff_included/omitted counts; it could also report the budget it derived and what consumed the rest, so a caller can see that its own 37KB contract cost it two source files. Worth a note in qa.md section 6p.1 too, since the umbrella case (R1-F6) is exactly where a caller is tempted to paste a large union payload.
